BMW’s i3 Touring Is an Electric Alternative to the Upcoming 3 Series Wagon – Spy Shots
15 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
BMW has so far used the i3 moniker on three different models, and the best-known was likely the original hatch . You know, the quirky-looking ride that hasn’t been a thing for a few years now.
That one was made between 2013 and 2022 at the Leipzig factory in Germany, and it is estimated that some 250,000 units have seen the light of day in total. Then came the electric sedan based on the G20 BMW 3 Series. The model was known as the G28, and it was assembled exclusively for the Chinese market between 2022 and 2026.
Fast forward to present day, and we have a brand new i3 in BMW’s portfolio. We are talking about the NA0 sports sedan, which is based on the Neue Klasse (NAx) platform. Thus, it shares plenty of components with the iX3. BMW unveiled it earlier this year, and production commenced at the Munich factory in Germany a couple of months ago. But so far, the family comprises a single member, the four-door sedan, and as we already know, the automaker is also working on its family-friendlier sibling.
Yep, that would be the BMW i3 Touring, which has been spied in the open on quite a few occasions. This model has also fallen into the hands of the pixel-altering crowd several times, as sketching it out is not that tricky. After all, you have to imagine a long-roof version of the i3 Sedan, with a tailgate opening up into a more generous cargo area, and you have the i3 Touring. This model will be offered as an electric alternative to the upcoming new-gen BMW 3 Series Touring, which is also in the making as we speak.
Photo: SH Proshots Mind you, you shouldn’t confuse the two, because even though they may look quite similar, both inside and out, the i3 is based on the Neue Klasse platform, as mentioned above, whereas the new 3er builds on an updated version of the CLAR construction. The G50 thus shares its nuts and bolts with its predecessor, as well as the G30 5 Series, the G32 6 Series, the G01 and G02 X3 and X4, respectively, the G29 Z4, Toyota’s GR Supra, the 4 Series, and other vehicles.
But we’re not here to talk about BMW’s modern-day compact lineup as a whole, as this story is all about the BMW i3 Touring. After all, a fresh batch of spy shots just ended up in our inbox again, as our vigilant man with the cam had a close encounter of the third kind with the tester as it was being pushed hard at the Nurburgring. And even though we have a very good idea of what it will look like, it still had its front and rear fascias under wraps.
Mind you, the front end will be virtually identical to that of its four-door sibling , and at the rear, it will feature the same taillights and bumper. In fact, the only differences between the two will be longer roofline of the Touring (Bimmer slang for station wagon), the larger rear three-quarter windows, the redesigned rear three-quarter panels, and a tailgate instead of a trunk lid. We also expect a few chassis tweaks, probably with an emphasis on the rear-axle suspension.
Photo: SH Proshots This prototype seems to sit on 20-inch wheels that spin around the red brake calipers, and appears to sport bumpers that are bit more aggressive. Thus, we could be looking at an M Sport model. The interior will carry over from the BMW i3 Sedan, complete with the Panoramic iDrive, the quirky-looking infotainment system, the four-spoke steering wheel, and so on. The rear headroom, however, and the cargo area behind the passenger compartment have been improved compared to the four-door model.
To no one’s surprise, the powertrain family will also carry over. This includes the 40 xDrive, with its 369 brake horsepower, and an 82.8 kWh battery pack that enables a 441-mile (710 km) on the WLTP cycle. The 50 xDrive offers 463 brake horsepower on tap, and has a 108.7 kWh battery pack that increases the range to 567 miles (912 km). Due to the different aerodynamic and presumably more weight, the i3 Touring should offer a slightly lower range, and will probably be a tiny bit less agile.
Both the BMW i3 Touring and the 3 Series Touring are expected to come out of hiding sometime in 2027, and they will launch in Europe shortly after the big unveiling. We wouldn’t hold our breath for the two premium compact station wagon models to make their way to the United States of America, because these things do not necessarily sell like hotcakes over here. But assuming they would, would you really buy one of these over an equivalent crossover? Feel free to tell us all about it in the comments area below.
